subject: Post-demo follow-up: exit origins, preferred serving topology, and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@finovate.ai>
Cc: Sally Chen <sallyc@healthsync.io>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: exit origins, preferred serving topology, and next steps

Hi Amit / Sally,

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning — appreciated the pragmatic questions. Quick recap and the 3 asks I promised: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary goal: replace an aging in-house serving stack to reduce ops overhead and cut per-token cost.
- Current origin: self-hosted Triton on an internal Slurm/GPU cluster; some traffic still going to a legacy API.
- Performance pain: warm-start latency variability during bursts; KV caching would help.
- Security: must meet bank-level controls; VPC or on-prem options preferred for high-sensitivity pipelines.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the migration sources (Triton endpoints vs legacy API) and approximate daily RPS per source? A short CSV is perfect.
2) Which deployment mode is your primary preference if cost/latency tradeoffs are neutral: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput), or Private VPC/on-prem (controls + compliance)?
3) Are there procurement or internal vendor review milestones we should align on (SOW, security questionnaire, procurement lead)?

I'll follow up internally and loop in our solutions engineer for a tech deep-dive once we have the CSV.

Attached: a short SLA sketch for Dedicated (high level).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Amit Shah <amit@finovate.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sally Chen <sallyc@healthsync.io>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: exit origins, preferred serving topology, and next steps

Jordan,

Thanks for the recap — very helpful. Quick answers inline.

Recap confirmation: correct on all points. A couple of clarifications:
- Migration sources: primary is our Triton cluster (internal hostnames, ~1200 endpoints) and a legacy REST API used by a small subset of customers (~15% traffic).
- Traffic: average 6k requests/day today, peak ~650 rps (short bursts during batch jobs). Most traffic is low concurrency but spikes matter.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for short-form generation; bindings currently miss during warm cache events.
- Security: finance product requires VPC + customer-managed KMS.

Primary preference: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering (predictable throughput + control). If a conservative cost estimate for Dedicated + VPC looks within 20% of our current op-ex, we will push for that. Hosted API is acceptable for low-sensitivity features while we validate quality.

Procurement: procurement lead is Sally (cc'd) — we need a draft SOW and our legal team will run a vendor risk assessment (SOC2 evidence required).

I've attached a simple inventory CSV (finovate-service-inventory.csv) with endpoints and per-endpoint RPS averages.

--
Amit Shah
Head of Platform
Finovate.ai
amit@finovate.ai | +1 212-555-0189

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: exit origins, preferred serving topology, and next steps

Thanks Amit — this is great and very actionable. Internal notes (cc'ing Grace and Sean to coordinate):

Grace / Sean — Finovate prefers Dedicated capacity behind a VPC peering + customer-managed KMS. They have ~6k req/day and 650 rps bursts; priority SLO 95th <= 220ms. They’re migrating from Triton + a legacy REST API. Attach inventory CSV they sent.

Proposed next steps from Redwood side:
- Grace: prep a Dedicated cost sketch + 12/36 month reserved options, include approximate add-on for VPC peer bandwidth and KMS key access overhead.
- Sean: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with the Finovate infra team to walk through KV caching/latency characteristics and required peering setup. Please include our infra engineer who owns KV caching.
- Jordan: I'll send an initial SOW skeleton and SLA sketch they can feed to procurement/legal.

Amit / Sally: available slots from our infra team — Tue 5/11 10am-11am PT, Wed 5/12 9am-10am PT, or Thu 5/13 1pm-2pm PT. Which works for you?

Jordan

Amit — see you on the call.
